A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EditCoT research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, locality tests, and efficiency and sensitivity analyses for EditCoT.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds RAG comparisons, expanded ablations, a fine-tuning control, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same answer generation, retrieval, conflict detection, iterative CoT editing, and HotpotQA training-data construction procedures. The cross-entropy loss statement and expanded prompts clarify implementation without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: v2 removes both DUNE debiasing splits from the evaluation and benchmark statistics, reducing DUNE coverage from five subsets to three and eliminating bias-reduction tasks. MQuAKE, the remaining DUNE tasks, LeKUBE, and HotpotQA training coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds RAT and FLARE to the MQuAKE/DUNE comparisons and the efficiency comparison, substantially expanding evaluation against advanced retrieval methods. Existing comparators remain in corresponding retained experiments; RAG is renamed Naive RAG.

E3.justification: Retained experiments preserve their principal metrics, sample counts, and training budget. Bounded additions include HotpotQA fine-tuning of Llama-3 for a control experiment, extra model/task configurations for component ablations, and RAT/FLARE settings, including FLARE's 0.12 threshold.

E4.justification: Component ablations expand from Qwen on MQuAKE to include Llama on MQuAKE and Qwen on LeKUBE MCQ. Appendices H and I add a training-knowledge control and two failure analyses, including observations from 200 manually inspected examples. Earlier successful cases and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new approximate failure counts are descriptive error-analysis results, not a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched main-table scores remain unchanged, including EditCoT's MQuAKE scores of 35.4 and 34.2. v2 adds RAT/FLARE results, expanded ablation and fine-tuning-control results, and failure findings while removing debiasing scores. The headline win count changes from 7/12 to 6/8 with the narrowed coverage.

T1.justification: The editor mapping, training-data tuple, prefix construction, and assumption about a single divergence are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims remain task-agnostic knowledge updating through CoT editing, preservation of the reasoning model, and strong effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency across tasks. v2 clarifies one-time editor training, which was already described in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of RAG shortcomings, reasoning-path conflicts, and failures caused by retrieval/conflict detection or faulty initial reasoning. It interprets the new fine-tuning control and expands the existing GPU-resource limitation with discussion of smaller proxy editors and unexplored compression.

D1.justification: Appendix J adds initial-answer and initial-CoT templates and replaces abbreviated examples with complete five-shot prompts for conflict detection and final answering. v2 also specifies cross-entropy training, Transformers use, new baseline settings, and licensing. The code/data URL is retained, although the explicit MS MARCO retriever-training detail is omitted.

R1.justification: New RAT, FLARE, and contrastive/context-aware decoding references accompany substantial positioning against RAG in Appendix C. The related-work survey is shortened, including removal of MEMIT, PAL, and Program of Thoughts discussions. The existing Verify-and-Edit comparison moves to Appendix B.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and results undergo extensive condensation and rewriting. Detailed comparisons, efficiency discussion, and case studies move into appendices, and limitations become a separate section. Authorship and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different document template, typography, and caption style. Table 1 is transposed and grouped by method family, LeKUBE becomes a separate table, the efficiency plot gains comparators, and new control/failure tables appear. Existing diagrams and case-study displays are reformatted or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added RAG comparisons, broader ablations, failure analyses, and fuller prompts improve experimental scrutiny and reproducibility. However, removing both DUNE debiasing splits reduces evidence for the retained broad generalization claims, and the fine-tuning control only indirectly addresses leakage. These tradeoffs limit the overall gain.
